```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)
theme_set(theme_bw(18))

cod <- read_csv("../data/pacific-cod-growth.csv") |>
  mutate(
    temp = factor(temp),
    co2 = factor(co2, levels = c("ambient", "high"))
  )
crabs <- read_csv("../data/spider-crab-development.csv") |>
  mutate(temp = factor(temp), co2 = factor(co2))
oysters <- read_csv("../data/oyster-shell-strength.csv") |>
  mutate(
    temp = factor(temp, levels = c("control", "warm")),
    co2 = factor(co2, levels = c("ambient", "750 ppm", "1000 ppm"))
  )

# Compare the additive and interactive models and format the result as a subtitle
f_label <- function(additive, interactive) {
  comparison <- anova(additive, interactive)
  p_value <- comparison$`Pr(>F)`[2]
  sprintf(
    "F = %.2f, p %s",
    comparison$F[2],
    if (p_value < 0.001) "< 0.001" else sprintf("= %.2f", p_value)
  )
}

# The same dodged boxplots and jittered points students make in Step 1
plot_system <- function(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  shape,
  title,
  subtitle,
  xlab,
  ylab,
  legend
) {
  ggplot(data, aes({{ x }}, {{ y }}, shape = {{ shape }})) +
    geom_boxplot(
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
      width = 0.6,
      outlier.shape = NA
    ) +
    geom_point(
      position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.5, dodge.width = 0.8),
      alpha = 0.6
    ) +
    labs(
      x = xlab,
      y = ylab,
      shape = legend,
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle
    ) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15))
}
```

# Model comparison

## Today's agenda

- **Review** how to compare models with ANOVA (10 min)
- **Apply** ANOVA to a multiple stressor experiment in groups (35 min)
- **Teach** your system to a jigsaw group (15 min)
- **Recap** the F statistic and ANOVA (10 min)

# Review: comparing models with ANOVA

## A warming experiment

Eelgrass shoot growth in tanks across a range of temperatures, at three nutrient levels: low (reference), medium, and high.

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Additive: } \text{growth} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{temp} + \beta_2 (\text{Medium}) + \beta_3 (\text{High}) + \epsilon \\
\text{Interactive: } \text{growth} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{temp} + \beta_2 (\text{Medium}) + \beta_3 (\text{High}) \\
&\quad + \beta_4 (\text{temp} \times \text{Medium}) + \beta_5 (\text{temp} \times \text{High}) + \epsilon
\end{align}
$$

:::

We want to know: does the effect of temperature depend on nutrients?

## What are $H_0$ and $H_A$?

::: {style="font-size:0.7em"}

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Additive: } \text{growth} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{temp} + \beta_2 (\text{Medium}) + \beta_3 (\text{High}) + \epsilon \\
\text{Interactive: } \text{growth} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{temp} + \beta_2 (\text{Medium}) + \beta_3 (\text{High}) \\
&\quad + \beta_4 (\text{temp} \times \text{Medium}) + \beta_5 (\text{temp} \times \text{High}) + \epsilon
\end{align}
$$

:::

::: {style="font-size:0.75em"}

**A.** $H_0$: $\beta_1 = \beta_2 = \beta_3 = \beta_4 = \beta_5 = 0$ $\qquad$ $H_A$: at least one $\neq 0$

[**B.** $H_0$: $\beta_4 = \beta_5 = 0$ $\qquad$ $H_A$: at least one of $\beta_4, \beta_5 \neq 0$]{.fragment .highlight-green fragment-index=1}

**C.** $H_0$: $\beta_4 = \beta_5 = 0$ $\qquad$ $H_A$: $\beta_4 \neq 0$ and $\beta_5 \neq 0$

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1 style="font-size:0.75em"}

- $H_0$ sets only the _extra_ coefficients to 0, which gives the additive model.
- $H_A$ is the opposite of $H_0$, so it only takes _one_ non-zero coefficient (not C).
- A compares the interactive model to `growth ~ 1`, so it doesn't ask about the interaction.

:::

## Which pair of models is nested?

::: {style="font-size:0.75em"}

**A.** `growth ~ temp` and `growth ~ nutrients`

[**B.** `growth ~ temp + nutrients` and `growth ~ temp * nutrients`]{.fragment .highlight-green fragment-index=1}

**C.** `growth ~ temp + nutrients` and `growth ~ temp * salinity`

**D.** `growth ~ nutrients` and `growth ~ temp + salinity`

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1 style="font-size:0.75em"}

Model A is **nested** in model B if setting some of B's coefficients to 0 gives you A.

- In B, set the interaction coefficients to 0 and you get the additive model.
- Sharing a predictor isn't enough. In C, no coefficients you could set to 0 turn `temp * salinity` into a model with `nutrients`.

:::

## Which scenario would use ANOVA?

Nutrients has 3 levels. Salinity is continuous.

::: {style="font-size:0.7em"}

**A.** Is temperature or nutrients the better predictor? <br/> `growth ~ temp` vs. `growth ~ nutrients`

**B.** Does salinity matter, accounting for temperature? <br/> `growth ~ temp` vs. `growth ~ temp + salinity`

[**C.** Does the effect of temperature depend on nutrients? <br/> `growth ~ temp + nutrients` vs. `growth ~ temp * nutrients`]{.fragment .highlight-green fragment-index=1}

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1 style="font-size:0.7em"}

- A isn't nested, so ANOVA can't compare the models.
- B is nested but adds one coefficient, so the p-value for that coefficient is sufficient.
- C is nested and adds two coefficients. No single p-value covers both.

:::

# Multiple stressors

## Stressors don't arrive one at a time

The ocean is warming _and_ acidifying. An experiment on one stressor can't tell us what happens when they combine.

::: {.incremental}

- **Additive**: each stressor has its own effect, and the combined effect is their sum
- **Interactive**: the effect of one stressor is _amplified_ or _reduced_ by the other
- Which one is it? That's a comparison of nested models.

:::

## Three experiments

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}

| System | Stressors | Response | Reference |
|-----|-----|-----|---|
| [Pacific cod larvae](../labs/week6-wednesday-cod.qmd) | Temperature × CO2 | Growth rate in dry mass | @slesinger2024 |
| [Spider crab larvae (_Hyas araneus_)](../labs/week6-wednesday-crabs.qmd) | Temperature × CO2 | Larval development time | @walther2010 |
| [Pacific oysters](../labs/week6-wednesday-oysters.qmd) | Temperature × CO2 | Shell strength | @lemasson2021 |

:::

All real data, all factorial experiments: every level of one stressor is crossed with every level of the other.

## Round 1: one system (35 min)

Form groups of 3-4. Each group takes one system and opens its page.

::: {style="font-size:0.75em"}

1. Visualize the data
2. Decide on the simpler and complex models
3. Fit both models
4. Compare the models using ANOVA
5. Interpret

:::

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.85em"}

Everyone in your group needs to be able to explain your results. You'll present them without your group.

:::

## Round 2: jigsaw (15 min)

Form new groups with at least one person from each system.

::: {.incremental style="font-size:0.9em"}

- Take **3 minutes** per system: the system, the models, your plot, and F, p, and your interpretation
- As a group, discuss:
  - How much did the evidence for interaction vary across scenarios?
  - If you did a follow-up study and did not find a significant interaction between temperature and CO2, would you decide to use the additive or interactive model?

:::

# Recap

## Three systems, three answers

```{r}
#| label: three-systems
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-align: center

cod_f <- f_label(
  lm(growth ~ temp + co2, cod),
  lm(growth ~ temp * co2, cod)
)
crabs_f <- f_label(
  lm(dev_time ~ temp + co2, crabs),
  lm(dev_time ~ temp * co2, crabs)
)
oysters_f <- f_label(
  lm(shell_strength ~ co2 + temp, oysters),
  lm(shell_strength ~ co2 * temp, oysters)
)

patchwork::wrap_plots(
  plot_system(
    cod,
    temp,
    growth,
    co2,
    "Pacific cod",
    cod_f,
    "Temperature (°C)",
    "Growth (%/day)",
    "CO2"
  ),
  plot_system(
    crabs,
    temp,
    dev_time,
    co2,
    "Spider crab",
    crabs_f,
    "Temperature (°C)",
    "Zoea II development time (days)",
    "CO2 (ppm)"
  ),
  plot_system(
    oysters,
    co2,
    shell_strength,
    temp,
    "Pacific oysters",
    oysters_f,
    "CO2 treatment",
    "Shell strength (N)",
    "Temperature"
  )
)
```

Each model comparison is additive vs. interactive.

## What's the F statistic?

$$
F = \frac{(RSS_{simple} - RSS_{complex}) \ / \ (p_{complex} - p_{simple})}{RSS_{complex} \ / \ (n - p_{complex})}
$$

::: {.incremental style="font-size:0.85em"}

- **Numerator**: the unexplained variation removed per coefficient added
- **Denominator**: the unexplained variation left per residual degree of freedom
- $F$ asks: are the new coefficients worth what they cost?
- $F \approx 1$ is about what we'd expect if the new coefficients explained only noise. Cod had $F = 0.27$; spider crab had $F = 61.67$.

:::

## When do we use ANOVA?

To compare two models when:

::: {.incremental}

- The response is **continuous**
- The models are **nested**: setting some coefficients in the complex model to 0 gives the simpler model
- They differ by **more than one coefficient**

:::

::: {.fragment}

Today, each interaction cost 2 or 4 coefficients. With one, use the p-value for that coefficient instead.

:::

## How do we interpret the results?

The p-value is the probability of an F at least this large _if the extra coefficients were all 0_.

::: {.incremental style="font-size:0.8em"}

- **p < 0.05** (spider crab): reject $H_0$. We have evidence that at least one extra coefficient isn't 0. The effect of CO2 depends on temperature.
- **p > 0.05** (oysters): fail to reject at $\alpha = 0.05$. A future study with a larger sample size could resolve the question one way or the other
- **p >> 0.05** (cod): fail to reject $H_0$. These results do not provide evidence that the effect of temperature depends on CO2.

:::
